name: cmd-shift-w-closes-the-selected-window
description: Two windows on the SAME space, both showing its tabs. Cmd+Shift+W must close the one the user selected and leave the other alone. close-window-tabless.json covers the single tabless window; this covers the half that decides WHICH window goes, which a one-window scenario cannot say anything about. Cmd+N seeds the new slot from the invoking window's space (CreateWindowSlot's seed_from_slot), so both sidebars render the same two tabs and the surviving one can be read back without knowing which window it is.

actions.note: let the startup space's live tab commit and the sidebar draw its rows
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
VACUITY GUARD. Both windows show the same space, so this reads 2 whichever sidebar target CDP picks - and a 0 here would mean the row assertion after the close proves nothing about tabs surviving.
SECOND WINDOW on the same space. It takes key focus, so it is the SELECTED window for the chord below.

actions.pattern: Atrium: Cmd\+N opened window-slot .* for host
actions.note: GATES THE WHOLE SCENARIO AS TWO-WINDOW. A Cmd+N that silently failed would leave one window here and the close below would be the tabless case again, reported as two-window coverage. Pattern carries no single quote - wait_vlog interpolates it into a single-quoted remote shell string.

the new window auto-opens its command palette (CreateWindowSlot's open_command_bar), and an Escape sent before that palette has KEY does nothing - measured at 14s from Cmd+N to 'command bar gained key' on this VM. Same 8s wait close-window-tabless.json needs for the startup palette.
first dismiss attempt. Undismissed, the palette owns the keyboard and the chord below never reaches a browser window.
second dismiss attempt: a press on the palette's scrim, the same path the Escape takes. Escape alone is unreliable here, which is why every sibling scenario backs it with this click.
GATE: the palette really went. The startup window has a restored tab and opens no palette of its own, so this line can only be the second window's.
names the selected window rather than trusting where key focus landed after the palette closed. Both windows are centred on the same spot, so this hits the frontmost - the new one.
let the close commit and the survivor settle
one window is left, so exactly one sidebar target remains for CDP to pick
evidence that what is left is a real window with its sidebar, not a husk

assertions.label: chord-reached-a-window
assertions.note: separates 'a window is still standing' from 'the chord never arrived', which is the ambiguity that let this task's AC be checked against a scenario that had never run its own assertions

assertions.label: only-one-window-was-asked-to-close
assertions.note: THE MEASUREMENT, the half a window count cannot make: the chord closed ONE window. Two lines would mean it walked the space's windows.
the guard's own reading, kept as an assertion so a fixture change that empties the space fails here rather than making rows-after meaningless
the surviving window still shows the space's two tabs. A window close is not a space delete, so the cold rows stay in the model.

assertions.label: the-survivors-tab-was-not-closed
assertions.note: the second window has no tab of its own, so closing it must close no tab at all. A line here would mean the chord reached across to the other window's live tab.

assertions.desc: LIVENESS: one window really gone, one really still on screen. min_area 200000 skips the phantom AXUnknown entry quit-two-windows.json recorded.
